papers.title: Reconstruction and well-posedness of an inverse coefficient problem for a diffusion equation
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the inverse coefficient problem of determining an unknown coefficient in a diffusion equation from a single boundary flux measurement. More precisely, assuming that the domain is cylindrical, we develop a unified theoretical and numerical framework for the stable reconstruction of a space-time-dependent coefficient, by reformulating the inverse problem as a nonlinear equation. The inherent nonlinearity of the problem is transferred to an auxiliary nonlinear equation, enabling the application of techniques and concepts from nonlinear analysis. By combining representation formulas with regularity properties of solutions to diffusion equations, we extend to nonlinear inverse problems an approach that has so far been restricted to linear ones. The theoretical reconstruction procedure is complemented by a numerical analysis of the proposed method, including convergence and error estimates, as well as numerical experiments. The proposed reconstruction algorithm is directly inspired by the theoretical framework.

papers.title: Quantum estimates for classical polynomial optimization
papers.abstract: The problem of finding lower and upper bounds on multivariate homogeneous polynomials is both difficult and important given its applications to questions ranging from dynamical stability in complex potential landscapes to data analysis. From the standpoint of tensor eigenvalue theory, the question is equivalent to finding the smallest and the largest eigenvalues of the coefficient tensor corresponding to the given polynomial. Standard approaches outlined in the literature amount to running nonlinear iterations in search for the optimal rays along which the growth of the polynomial is fastest or slowest. Unlike the case of matrices (or their corresponding multivariate quadratic forms) convergence of such algorithms for higher-rank tensors is capricious due to the complex topography of polynomial objective functions. In this essay, a very different strategy, inspired by quantum-mechanical variational methods, is introduced for finding bounds on polynomials. The original polynomial is replaced by an operator acting in a suitably chosen (large) space of states, such that in an appropriate "classical" limit this operator approaches the original polynomial expression made of commutative variables. As a result, approximating the smallest and largest eigenvalues of the coefficient tensor, and thus finding bounds on polynomials, amounts to diagonalizing the resulting quantum operator, represented as a large matrix, and then inspecting the smallest and largest eigenvalues of this matrix. This approach is then successfully applied to standard test examples from tensor eigenvalue literature and other problems of interest in mathematical physics including Strichartz-type inequalities.

papers.title: Soft-confinement approximation of no-flux McKean-Vlasov dynamics
papers.abstract: We study the approximation of the no-flux McKean-Vlasov equation on a bounded convex domain by a whole-space equation with quadratic confinement of strength $\lambda^{-1}$ outside the domain. For a smooth bounded interaction kernel and a common bounded initial density with square-integrable gradient, we establish an $O(\lambda^{1/4})$ approximation rate. The estimate controls the $L^2$ density error uniformly on every finite time interval and the gradient error in space-time $L^2$. Without interaction, a spectral gap independent of $\lambda$ yields the $O(\lambda^{1/4})$ rate uniformly in time for the density error and uniformly over all unit time intervals for the gradient error. With interaction, we construct a counterexample showing that even weak convergence can fail to be uniform in time.

papers.title: On symmetry and monotonicity of singular solutions to critical fractional Hartree equations
papers.abstract: This paper continues the study initiated in \cite{GuJevnikarYang2026b} of fractional Hartree equations with zero capacity singular sets. We are concerned here with the critical case, i.e. \[ (-\Delta)^s u=\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma} \frac{u^{2_{\mu,s}^*}(y)}{|x-y|^\mu}\,d y\right)u^{2_{\mu,s}^*-1} \quad\text{in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\Gamma, \] where $N\ge2$, $s\in(0,1)$, $\mu\in(0,N)$ and $2_{\mu,s}^*$ is the critical exponent associated to this class of problems. We prove symmetry and monotonicity with respect to the singular set $\Gamma$. The Kelvin transforms centered at regular points provide sufficient decay at infinity for both the transformed solutions and their associated Hartree coefficients, without imposing global integrability assumptions. Combined with a moving plane argument and a comparison estimate in critical Lebesgue spaces, this allows the moving plane method to cover the full interaction range.

papers.title: One-third H\"older stability of optimal transport maps from log-concave sources
papers.abstract:
We prove quantitative stability of quadratic optimal transport maps from arbitrary log-concave sources to bounded targets. If the source $ho$ is isotropic on $\mathbb R^d$ and the targets $\mu$, $
u$ are supported in a common ball of radius $R$, their Brenier maps satisfy \[ \lVert T_\mu-T_
uVert_{L^2(ho)} \leqslant 17d^{2/3}R^{2/3}W_2(\mu,
u)^{1/3}. \] The one-third exponent is optimal for $d\geqslant2$. The proof combines a linear stability estimate for Brenier potentials in a weighted norm with a matching weighted reverse Poincar'e inequality. The weight is chosen in terms of the negative log-density of the source to account for its tails. We also show that the best dimensional constant in map stability is at least of order $d^{1/3}$.

papers.title: Continuity and Stability of the FitzHugh Nagumo System with Respect to the Diffusion
papers.abstract: Spatial heterogeneity in diffusion is a fundamental feature of excitable media, yet its effect on FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics remains mathematically challenging. We establish stability of solutions with respect to perturbations of the diffusion coefficient, providing a rigorous account of how changes in the medium affect the evolution of the system. Specifically, we prove a continuous dependence result ensuring that small perturbations in diffusion produce small variations in the corresponding solutions. The proof adapts the method of contracting rectangles to variable diffusion, yielding a framework for controlling and comparing solutions associated with different diffusion profiles. This result provides a rigorous link between heterogeneous and homogeneous FitzHugh Nagumo systems and justifies constant-diffusion approximations when the diffusion coefficient is close to a constant. Our analysis advances the understanding of FitzHugh Nagumo dynamics in heterogeneous media by establishing robustness with respect to spatial variations in diffusion.

papers.title: Existence of a Normalized Mountain Pass Solution for a Coupled Cubic Schr\"odinger System with Partial Confinement
papers.abstract: This paper studies a mass supercritical Schr\"odinger system with partial confinement: $$ \begin{cases} -\Delta u_1+|y|^2u_1 =\lambda_1u_1+\mu_1u_1^3+2\beta u_1u_2^2,\qquad x\in\R^3,\\ -\Delta u_2+|y|^2u_2 =\lambda_2u_2+\mu_2u_2^3+2\beta u_1^2u_2,\qquad x\in\R^3, \end{cases} $$ subject to the mass constraints $ \int_{\R^3}u_1^2\dd x=a_1$, $\int_{\R^3}u_2^2\dd x=a_2,$ where $x=(y,z)\in\R^2\times\R$, the parameters $\mu_1,\mu_2,\beta$ are positive, and $\lambda_1,\lambda_2\in\R$ are unknown Lagrange multipliers. The masses satisfy $(a_1,a_2)=\eps(\rho_1,\rho_2)$ for a fixed vector $\rho=(\rho_1,\rho_2)\in (0,\infty)^2$. For all sufficiently small $\eps>0$, we establish the existence of a positive normalized solution $u_\eps^-$ at a mountain pass level on the full product mass sphere. This level coincides with the infimum of the energy over the negative part of the Pohozaev set. The main difficulty arises from the lack of compactness due to partial confinement. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness argument that preserves the two independent mass constraints and show that every minimizing sequence for this infimum admits a strongly convergent subsequence after suitable common translations along the unconfined axial direction. We further establish the asymptotic relation $\eps E(u_\eps^-)\to m_0(\rho)$ as $\varepsilon\to0$, where $m_0(\rho)>0$ denotes the infimum of the free energy under the corresponding Pohozaev constraint. In addition, we derive the asymptotic behavior of the kinetic and potential energies. The solution obtained here is distinct from the normalized ground states constructed by Jia et al. [Discrete Contin. Dyn. Syst., 40(2020), 2739-2766] through local minimization for sufficiently small masses.

papers.title: Analysis of a Two Membrane Thermoelastic Problem
papers.abstract: We formulate and study a mathematical model of a thermoforming process involving two interdependent thermoelastic membranes coupled with equations governing heat transfer. These membranes interact with each other through means of elastic forces and thermal transfer which determines changes in elastic properties and further deform the membranes. The two thermoelastic membranes lead to a pair of implicit obstacle problems which are modeled both as a 2-membrane problem or a pair of quasi-variational inequalities. Mathematically, the primary model couples an elliptic two membrane problem with associated nonlinear elliptic equations describing temperature distribution. We show, under physically relevant conditions, the existence of solutions via a fixed point approach that involves reformulation of the problem to improve regularity of solutions.

papers.title: Observability and stabilizability for Grushin-Type parabolic equations in the whole space
papers.abstract: We study observability and stabilization for the whole-space Grushin heat equation $$ \partial_t u-\Delta_\gamma u=0,\qquad \Delta_\gamma:=\Delta_x+|x|^{2\gamma}\Delta_y,\qquad (t,x,y)\in(0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m,\quad \gamma>0. $$ For product sets $E=E_1\times E_2$, we identify three observability regimes in which thickness, distance from the degeneracy set $\{x=0\}$, and local density near that set play different roles. (i) In the subcritical regime $0<\gamma<1$, the observability inequality holds for every $T>0$ if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick; hence $T_{\min}(E)=0$. (ii) At the critical exponent $\gamma=1$, if $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ is thick, we determine the exact minimal observable time: $$ T_{\min}(E)=\frac{a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)^2}{2n},\qquad a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1):=\operatorname*{ess\,inf}_{x\in E_1}|x|. $$ Thus, the threshold depends on the essential distance of $E_1$ from the degeneracy set. (iii) In the supercritical regime $\gamma>1$, we consider $n=1$, $E_2=\mathbb{R}^m$ and thick sets $E_1\subset\mathbb{R}$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)>0$, observability fails for every $T>0$, so that $T_{\min}(E)=+\infty$. If $a_{\mathrm{ess}}(E_1)=0$, observability depends on the density of $E_1$ near $0$, measured by $$ D_{E_1}(r):=\log\!\left(\frac{2r}{|E_1\cap(-r,r)|}\right),\qquad L_{E_1}:=\limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^2D_{E_1}(r). $$ If $L_{E_1}=0$, then $T_{\min}(E)=0$; if $0<L_{E_1}<\infty$, a finite sufficient observation time exists. Moreover, observability at time $T$ requires $$ \limsup_{r\downarrow0}r^{2(1+\gamma)/(\gamma-1)}D_{E_1}(r)\le C_{T,\gamma}. $$ In contrast, for every $\gamma>0$, exponential and complete stabilizability hold if and only if both $E_1$ and $E_2$ are thick. The stabilization criterion is therefore independent of $\gamma$.

papers.title: Effect of a fourth-order diffusion term on the robustness of the transfer function stability for hyperbolic systems
papers.abstract: We study a $2\times2$ hyperbolic system with anti-located control and observation. It is well known that the system can be stabilized with a delayed output-feedback control and that, unfortunately, this design is arbitrarily sensitive to small errors in the transport velocity. It was recently proved that adding a second-order diffusion term to the system restores robustness. We show that the same phenomenon occurs with a fourth-order diffusion term: the maximal spectral abscissa of the closed-loop system converges, as the diffusion parameter goes to zero, to the explicit value $-\ln(2)$, and the resulting stability margin is robust to small perturbations of the transport velocity. This additional term leads to a quartic characteristic equation whose roots have no tractable closed-form expression. We develop an asymptotic classification of its four roots and use it to obtain a first-order expansion of the transfer function with an explicit error bound. Combining this expansion with a topological degree argument, we show that $-\ln(2)$ is in fact the exact limiting value of the spectral abscissa, extending to the fourth-order case the sharpness result previously available only for second-order diffusive terms.

papers.title: Failure of superharmonicity near an isolated singularity of the critical biharmonic equation
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge5$ and $u$ be a positive singular solution of $\Delta^2u=u^{(n+4)/(n-4)}$ in a punctured ball. A long-standing question is where or not $ -\Delta u>0$ in the punctured ball. In this paper we show that the answer is negative. More precisely we construct a positive singular solution whose singularity at the origin is nonremovable, while its lower limit there is zero. On a normal subspace, $-\Delta u$ converges to a strictly negative constant. The spherical minimum has order $r^\beta$, where $2<\beta<4$, and the spherical Harnack ratio is unbounded. The proof uses balanced planar polygons, finitely many exterior parameters and a countable gluing construction.

papers.title: The Maximum Principle and Optimal Gradient Estimates of Solutions to the Insulated Conductivity Problem
papers.abstract: We study the insulated conductivity problem with two unit spherical inclusions embedded in a bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge3$. The gradient of solutions may blow up as the distance between the two inclusions goes to zero. We introduce bispherical coordinates and expand the solution in spherical harmonics. Then we use the maximum principle to give a new proof of the optimal gradient estimate obtained by Dong-Li-Yang.

papers.title: Constrained minimization problem and unbounded dynamics for the four-dimensional Klein-Gordon-Schr\"{o}dinger System
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the Klein-Gordon-Schrodinger system in four spatial dimensions. We consider a constrained minimization problem associated with the corresponding stationary system and establish the existence of a positive radial minimizer. We further investigate the asymptotic behavior and qualitative properties of minimizers. As an application, we analyze the dynamics of solutions with initial data in a potential well and prove that such solutions either blow up in finite time or exhibit unbounded growth in the energy norm as time tends to infinity. Since the minimizers lie on the boundary of the potential well, we also establish the strong instability of the associated standing waves.

papers.title: A Viscous Cascade Construction of Nonunique Leray--Hopf Solutions to the Unforced 3D Navier--Stokes Equations
papers.abstract: We construct a nonzero divergence-free initial velocity on $\mathbb{R}^3$ and a continuum of pairwise distinct suitable Leray--Hopf solutions of the unforced three-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations on a common time interval. The initial datum is axisymmetric, smooth away from the origin, and belongs to every $L^{\mathfrak q}$ with $1\leq \mathfrak q<3$, but not to $L^3$. All the solutions attain this datum strongly in $L^2$, are smooth at positive times, and satisfy both the global and local energy equalities through time zero. The same family belongs simultaneously to every $L^{\mathfrak p}_tL^{\mathfrak q}_x$ with $1\leq \mathfrak p\leq\infty$, $2\leq \mathfrak q\leq\infty$, and $2/\mathfrak p+3/\mathfrak q>1$. The same solutions also belong to the critical Lorentz space $L^\infty_tL^{3,\infty}_x$. This endpoint is sharp for uniqueness in the Leray--Hopf class within the Lorentz scale. The proof is entirely analytic and uses a cascade through geometrically separated Gaussian swirls. We establish growth for the time-dependent viscous linearization and determine the sign of its complete quadratic stress, including the interaction of the reference velocity with the second variation. The integrated stress generates a controlled perturbation at the next larger spatial scale. At each finite cutoff, a prescribed terminal coordinate selects an initial perturbation whose physical $L^2$ norm tends to zero as the cutoff is removed. Uniform energy, moment, and transfer estimates yield the common strong initial trace while preserving a nonzero observable at a fixed positive time.

papers.title: Dispersion of Magnetic Coriolis Waves
papers.abstract: We consider the 3-D rotating magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) equations. The combination of rotation and background magnetic field leads to the occurrence of dispersive magneto-Coriolis waves in the linearized equations. We establish a t ^{-1} decay estimate for waves with dispersion relation $\sigma$($\xi$) = $\xi$ \_3 h(|$\xi$|) under suitable assumptions on h, and show that this includes magneto-Coriolis waves. Then we apply these dispersive estimates to the nonlinear rotating MHD equations and obtain an improved lower bound on the lifespan of solutions.

papers.title: Sharp asymptotic stability of the IPM equation in $\mathbb{R}^2$ via isopycnal coordinates
papers.abstract: We study the incompressible porous media (IPM) equation, a model describing the motion of a fluid with variable density through a porous medium under the action of gravity. We prove that the stably stratified state, in which heavier fluid lies below lighter fluid, is nonlinearly stable: small perturbations decay over time and the fluid returns to equilibrium. Our result holds in the sharp Sobolev setting $H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ for every $s>2$: this threshold cannot be improved, since the equation is ill-posed in $H^2(\mathbb R^2)$. This result follows from a proof of global well-posedness at critical Besov regularity, with smallness required only in a norm invariant under the natural scaling of the equation. We also prove optimal decay rates for suitably localized initial data. The main difficulty is that the stabilizing effect of stratification acts only in some directions, while the nonlinear transport acts in all of them. Reaching the sharp regularity threshold requires two main novelties. First, we rewrite the equation in \emph{isopycnal coordinates}, which follow the level sets of the density: in these coordinates the transport becomes one-dimensional, and the anisotropic stabilizing mechanism can be exploited at minimal regularity. Second, we establish new \emph{anisotropic commutator estimates} which allow us to control the remaining nonlinear terms. Finally, we show that the estimates obtained in isopycnal coordinates can be transferred back to the original variables.

papers.title: From Continuum-Kinematics-Inspired Peridynamics to Simplicial Hyperelasticity
papers.abstract: We develop a variational and functional-analytic framework for continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamics with simultaneous nonlocal interactions among multiple points. We encode the finite-difference data of each interacting simplex in a simplicial deformation gradient. For nondegenerate simplices in three dimensions, the gradient, its cofactor, and its determinant encode the associated continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic line, area, and volume changes, respectively. This unified representation leads to a class of simplicial hyperelastic energies with general, possibly nonadditive, constitutive dependence on the affine deformation of an interacting simplex, thereby extending the original continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic framework. To describe interactions occurring at different scales and over different simplex geometries, we introduce radial- and shape-weighted nonlocal spaces. Their multipoint seminorms control two-point energies induced by the edge marginals of the interaction measure. This comparison yields nonlocal Poincar\'e inequalities and fractional Sobolev embeddings. We establish existence of equilibrium configurations by two complementary mechanisms. Particle-wise averaged convexity yields weak lower semicontinuity of the associated energy functionals. Under stronger assumptions on the edge marginals, fractional compactness gives existence for nonconvex energy densities. These results provide a mathematical foundation for simplicial and continuum-kinematics-inspired peridynamic models.

papers.title: Classification of radially symmetric solutions to a Hardy-H{\'e}non equation with sublinear absorption and applications
papers.abstract: Uniqueness of a non-negative radially symmetric solution with non-increasing profile to the Hardy-H{\'e}non elliptic equation with sublinear absorption \\ ____________ $\Delta$v(x) + |x|\textsuperscript{$\sigma$}v(x) - v\textsuperscript{1/m}(x)=0, ______ x$\in$___\textsuperscript{N}, \\ is established in the range N$\ge$1, m>1 and $\sigma$$\in$(max{-2,-N},0). Consequences of this result are the uniqueness (up to scaling) of the non-negative extremal function to a Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality and the uniqueness of a non-negative radially symmetric self-similar solution with nonincreasing profile to a parabolic Hardy-H{\'e}non equation with quasilinear diffusion. The proof relies on ordinary differential equations techniques, which can be used thanks to the radially symmetric setting, and requires in particular a delicate analysis of the well-posedness and continuous dependence in view of the non-Lipschitz nonlinearity and the singularity of |x|\textsuperscript{$\sigma$} at the origin.

papers.title: Large time behavior of global solutions to one-dimensional non-isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations with large initial data
papers.abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with the construction of global solutions to the Cauchy problem for the one-dimensional non-isentropic compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations, as well as the precise description of their large-time behavior. While results for small initial data are well-established, the case of large initial perturbations remains less satisfactory. Even for constant transport coefficients, only the Nishida-Smoller type solutions have been obtained so far. In this work, we will provide a complete resolution of this problem. The key idea involves revealing favorable hidden identities of the potential force and a new representation for the specific volume, which enables us to derive uniform upper and lower bounds on this quantity. Moreover, this strategy extends to compressible viscous single-ion flow under the Boltzmann relation; notably, this new method for deriving lower and upper bounds on the specific volume also applies to the Navier-Stokes equations. The proof relies on a domain decomposition technique and some new dissipative structures to close the nonlinear energy estimates.

papers.title: Normal form smoothing and spatial analyticity for the dispersion-generalized periodic KdV equation
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the persistence of spatial analyticity for solutions to the dispersion-generalized periodic Korteweg-de Vries equation $$\partial_tu-\partial_x|D_x|^\alpha u+u\partial_xu=0,\qquad\alpha\ge2.$$ For real-valued initial data $u_0\in G^{\sigma_0,s}(\mathbb T)$, with $\sigma_0>0$ and $s\ge-\alpha/4$, we prove that the corresponding global solution satisfies $$u\in C([-T,T];G^{\sigma(T),s}(\mathbb T)),\qquad\sigma(T)=\min\left\{\sigma_0,\frac cT\right\},$$ for every $T>0$. As a consequence, our result improves the lower bound for the radius of spatial analyticity established by Himonas, Kalisch, and Selberg (2017) for $2\le\alpha<4$, including the classical periodic KdV equation, and establishes a unified $T^{-1}$ lower bound for the analyticity radius for every $\alpha\ge2$. The main novelties are twofold. First, we introduce a normal form reduction at the level of the Gevrey energy, which reveals an additional cancellation in the cubic Gevrey commutator and separates it into a non-accumulating boundary correction and a quartic remainder. Second, we establish a global-in-time periodic $L_{t,x}^4$ estimate for the non-polynomial phase $k|k|^\alpha$, valid for every real $\alpha\ge2$. Together, these ingredients yield a refined almost conservation law and the $T^{-1}$ lower bound for the radius of spatial analyticity.

papers.title: Generalized principal eigenvalues for nonlocal operators with drift
papers.abstract: Nonlocal diffusion operators with a drift term naturally arise in models such as moving coordinate systems induced by climate change. This paper systematically studies several concepts of generalized principal eigenvalues (GPEs) for such operators. We allow the dispersal kernel to be heterogeneous and non-symmetric, and remove the standard global upper bound on the kernel (thereby covering the case of heavy-tailed dispersal kernels). To overcome the analytical difficulties brought by this more general setting, we establish a new Harnack-type inequality for non-compactly supported kernels, and apply homogenization and cut-off approximation techniques to derive two-sided bounds for the domain approximation limit of GPEs. Furthermore, under the almost periodic setting, we prove that the GPEs defined through different admissible test function spaces (e.g., \(C^1\) spaces with bounded derivatives and uniformly continuous function spaces in the viscosity sense) are completely coincident. This characterization reveals a fundamental unification: the limit result of principal eigenvalues under domain approximation by Coville and Hamel coincides exactly with the explicit variational formula by Du, Fang, and Ni, thereby bridging two previously independent theoretical results.

papers.title: Second critical exponent for a quasilinear Hardy--H\'enon equation
papers.abstract: We study the Cauchy problem for the parabolic Hardy--H\'enon equation $\partial_tu=\Delta u^m+|x|^\sigma u^p$ with slow diffusion $m>1$ and a potential which is singular at the origin, $-2<\sigma<0$, in dimension $N\ge3$. Above the Fujita exponent, global and blowing-up solutions coexist, and we show that the spatial decay of the initial data decides between them. The second critical exponent turns out to be the decay rate of an explicit singular steady state. Data decaying more slowly blow up in finite time, whatever their size, while faster decaying data which are small in a weighted supremum norm give rise to global solutions. At the critical decay, and in the range where the singular steady state exists, we construct bounded stationary barriers with exactly critical tail by gluing the singular steady state to regular steady states. We deduce that the critical amplitude separating global existence from blow-up lies between the amplitude of the singular steady state and an explicit constant. We also show that data lying below a proper fraction of the singular steady state produce global bounded solutions, and that the singular amplitude itself is attained by global solutions whenever a Joseph--Lundgren type condition fails. Conjectures and open problems complete the picture.

papers.title: One-dimensional nodal solutions of the Lane--Emden problem in cylinders: asymptotic behaviour and energy stability
papers.abstract: We consider the Lane-Emden problem $-\Delta u=|u|^{p-1}u$, $p>1$, in bounded domains of a half-cylinder $\omega\times(0,+\infty)$, with Dirichlet conditions on the relative boundary and Neumann conditions on the boundary of the cylinder. In flat cylinders $\omega\times(0,L)$ this problem admits, for every $p>1$, one-dimensional solutions with any prescribed number $m$ of nodal regions. We study the stability of these domains, as critical points of a related energy functional, with respect to volume-preserving deformations of the domain. We prove that, for $p$ large, the flat cylinders are stable as soon as their height exceeds a threshold growing linearly in $p$, while, for $p$ close to $1$, both stability and instability occur, with explicit thresholds depending on $m$ and on the first nontrivial Neumann eigenvalue of $\omega$. These results rely on a detailed analysis of the one-dimensional profiles: we describe their asymptotic behaviour, and that of the first eigenvalue of the associated linearized operator, as $p\to1^+$ and $p\to+\infty$, we obtain expansions of the amplitude with explicit constants, and we prove global comparison results with respect to $p$, some of which are new also for positive solutions.

papers.title: The Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators in divergence form
papers.abstract:
We establish the Kato square root property for fractional elliptic operators $L = -\operatorname{div}^\alpha(\mu 
abla^\alpha \cdot)$ of order $2\alpha \in (0,2)$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, built from the Riesz fractional gradient and divergence, with bounded, measurable and uniformly elliptic complex coefficients $\mu$. More precisely, we show that the domain of $L^{1/2}$ coincides with the distributional fractional Sobolev space $\mathrm{S}^{\alpha,2}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ and that $\|L^{1/2} u\|_{\mathrm{L}^2} \simeq \|
abla^\alpha u\|_{\mathrm{L}^2}$, with constants that are locally uniform in $\alpha$. As a consequence, we recover the Kato square root property for elliptic operators $-\operatorname{div}(\mu
abla\cdot)$ in the limit $\alpha 	o 1$, and we obtain continuity of the square root with respect to the parameter $\alpha$. The proof follows the second-order approach to the Kato problem. Its two new ingredients are nonlocal off-diagonal estimates of polynomial order for the resolvents of $L$, and a construction of $T(b)$-test functions that circumvents the nonlocality of $
abla^\alpha$ by factorizing it through Riesz potentials.

papers.title: Positive coexistence solutions for systems of multi-kernel Hammerstein type equations
papers.abstract: We investigate positive solutions with both components nontrivial for systems of Hammerstein integral equations associated with a general $2\times2$ matrix of Green's kernels, thereby extending the decoupled (diagonal) case to systems with cross-coupling. Such systems arise from boundary value problems in which the unknowns may be coupled both in the differential equations and in the boundary conditions, a setting that has received considerably less attention than the decoupled case. Using a component-wise Krasnosel'ski\u{\i} compression--expansion fixed point theorem in product cones, we derive existence and non-existence criteria. A multiplicity result guaranteeing at least two positive solutions is also obtained, by means of the fixed point index in cones. As an application, we consider radially symmetric solutions for an elliptic system on an annulus with coupled Robin boundary conditions.

papers.title: Asymptotic behavior of generic Riemann solutions to one-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the time-asymptotic stability of the one-dimensional full compressible Navier-Stokes-Poisson equations, assuming that the corresponding quasi-neutral Euler equations admit a generic Riemann solution consisting of a shock, a contact discontinuity, and a rarefaction wave. It is proved that there exists a unique global-in-time solution, which converges in $L^\infty$ norm, as time goes to infinity, to the ansatz composed of a viscous shock with a time-dependent shift, a viscous contact wave, and an inviscid rarefaction wave. The main difficulty arises from the non-conservative lower-order source terms induced by the electric potential in the momentum and energy equations, which significantly complicates the proof of the existence of individual waves (especially the viscous shock) and the derivation of the relative entropy estimates. To overcome this, we make full use of the Poisson equation satisfied by the electric potential, and combine the weighted relative entropy method with the $a$-contraction method with shifts to close the estimates within the $H^2$-perturbation framework.

papers.title: Construction of entropies for cross-diffusion systems
papers.abstract: The analysis of cross-diffusion systems with nonsymmetric and indefinite diffusion matrices often relies on the existence of entropies, that is, Lyapunov functionals whose dissipation often yields gradient estimates. We propose a general strategy for constructing entropies for two-species cross-diffusion systems, based on the assumption that the mobility matrix is symmetric, in accordance with Onsager's reciprocal relations. The symmetry condition leads to a linear hyperbolic equation in two variables, which can be reformulated as a linear transport system along the eigendirections of the diffusion matrix, related to the approach of Jenssen and Kogan for hyperbolic conservation laws. Positive solutions to this system yield a family of entropies parametrized by two arbitrary functions of one variable. Sufficient conditions for their existence on (possibly unbounded) characteristic rectangles are given, the mechanisms that may prevent the existence of an entropy are identified, and systems without any entropy structure are presented. The general construction recovers known entropies for models arising in physics and biology and provides new ones. For systems with an arbitrary number of components, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of separable entropies and give a rank criterion for the uniqueness of entropies (up to affine functions). Cross-diffusion systems without symmetry of the mobility matrix are also discussed.

papers.title: Unique continuation, nonexistence and bubbling for the critical $p$-Laplace equation II: the degenerate elliptic case and higher dimensions
papers.abstract:
For every $p>1$, we prove that a nontrivial solution of  egin{equation*} -\Delta_pu=f(x,u,
abla u) \end{equation*} in a planar domain, with $|f(x,s,\xi)|\leq C(|s|^{p-1}+|\xi|^{p-1})$, vanishes neither on an open set nor to infinite order at a point. This allows us to prove unique continuation properties of axially symmetric solutions to $p$-Laplace equations in higher dimensions $N\geq3$, with axially symmetric $p$-harmonic functions as a particular case. Unlike in our previous work, the analysis is based here on the regularity and quasiconformal properties of the whole stress field $|
abla u|^{p-2}
abla u$ in the plane, taking into account the more delicate regularity theory for $p>2$. This allows us to prove Liouville-type and bubble profile decomposition results for critical problems in dimensions $N\geq3$ and in the whole range $1<p<N$, under some symmetry conditions.

papers.title: Evolution Dynamics and Cauchy Problems with Quaternionic Variables and Lifting to Banach Bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-Algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a theory of evolution dynamics in a Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-algebra and establish a well-posedness theory for the Cauchy problem of evolution equations with quaternionic variables. First, we study the geometric properties of slice structures of Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-modules. By employing different slice structures, we construct some noncommutative Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-subalgebras which are compatible with the slice regularity of the functions involved. Moreover, through the quaternionic sliced geometric path integral over Banach bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-module, an integral representation of the solution to the homogeneous Cauchy problem with quaternionic variables is obtained in a quaternionic $\sigma$-ball, and for the first time, a local existence and uniqueness theorem is established for $\sigma$-analytic solutions. Then the local $\sigma$-analytic solution is extended to the entire quaternionic spherical sectorial region, thereby proving a global existence and uniqueness theorem for the Cauchy problem. Based on it, the notion of an evolution system in a quaternionic $\mathbb{H}$-algebra is introduced and its core properties are established. In addition, the global existence and uniqueness theorems are obtained under hyperbolic-like and parabolic-like conditions. Finally, the structure of Banach bilateral $\mathbb{H}$-modules and $\mathbb{H}$-algebras is lifted to Banach bilateral $\mathbb{A}$-modules and $\mathbb{A}$-algebras, and a well-posedness theory for evolution equations in this setting is developed. This reveals, from a new perspective, the universality of well-posedness for the Cauchy problem under the generic noncommutative $\mathbb{A}$-algebraic structures.

papers.title: Finite-Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes with Smooth Forcing, Part II: Residual Correction via Oscillatory Pulses
papers.abstract: This paper is a companion to Part I: Construction of Self-Similar Solutions with Admissible Stress and Flat Remainder (arXiv:2609.35406). Part I constructs approximately self-similar flow profiles with a singular stress in divergence form. The associated velocity becomes unbounded as $t\uparrow 1$. Here, localized oscillatory pulses cancel this stress contribution through their averaged quadratic momentum flux. Successive corrections preserve the velocity growth and leave a smooth external force $f\in C^\infty$. This gives a local solution of the three-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with forcing $f$. Its velocity satisfies $\limsup_{t\uparrow 1}\|u(t)\|_{L^\infty}=\infty$. Together, the two papers present a readable and accessible account of OpenAI's Finite Time Blowup for Navier-Stokes. We claim no original mathematical contribution.
